snippets.text: TikTok says its new Shopping Assistant is a conversational agent that remembers preferences and answers questions on sizing, shipping and availability, alongside one-click Buy Direct checkout from the For You feed, TechCrunch reports.
snippets.why: The aim is to keep shoppers inside TikTok instead of sending product questions to outside chatbots such as ChatGPT.

snippets.text: Instinct says its AI agent now works in group chats, letting friends plan trips and carpools together, even those without an account, with personal agents needing permission before sharing information or acting, TechCrunch reports.
snippets.why: Shared agents in group chats test whether assistants can work for several people without leaking what each person told them privately.

snippets.text: RemoveMacAI, an open-source command-line tool on GitHub, deletes about 12GB of Apple Intelligence models that macOS 27 keeps on disk even with every AI setting off, The Verge reports.
snippets.why: The Verge says macOS 27 dropped the single Settings toggle for disabling Apple Intelligence, leaving the models on disk.

snippets.text: Android Authority reports an app teardown shows Google may extend Gemini's Call for Me beyond business calls, with examples such as 'Call Mom and tell her I will be 15 minutes late'.
snippets.why: It is a teardown of unreleased code, so the feature and its wording may change or never ship.

snippets.text: Ars Technica reports that trust gaps in the MCP agent-to-agent protocol let malicious prompts spread from one agent to another, including in agents from Google and others.
snippets.why: If one compromised agent can pass instructions to the next, a single poisoned message could travel through a whole chain of tools.

snippets.text: AI developer omarsar0 says he built a proactive personal agent on the open-source Pi Durable, which checkpoints every step so he can kill it mid-task and it resumes where it stopped.
snippets.why: Durable checkpointing is the kind of plumbing that lets agents run unattended on schedules without losing work to a crash.

snippets.text: OpenAI's developer account posted a video showing how to start tasks by voice, manage agents across projects and branch into separate worktrees with the Codex command-line tool.
snippets.why: Voice-started tasks and parallel worktrees show OpenAI pushing Codex toward running several coding agents at once from the terminal.

snippets.text: Aleph Alpha says its Kolibri-1, a German-English mixture-of-experts model with 78 billion parameters and about 3 billion active per token, is out under Apache 2.0, with a context window up to one million tokens.
snippets.why: It is a European-built open-weights model trained on 768 B200 GPUs, pitched at public administration and industry as a sovereignty play; the model card dates the release to 3 October.

snippets.text: Artificial Analysis says ElevenLabs' Eleven v4 Turbo now ranks first on its Provider Voice text-to-speech arena with an Elo of 1,334, ahead of Eleven v4 at 1,321, at half the price.
snippets.why: The ranking rests on 1,645 appearances, and it puts a cheaper model ahead of ElevenLabs' own flagship sibling.

snippets.text: Z.ai says GLM-5.3 is now available on Amazon Bedrock, pitching it to enterprises for coding and agentic work.
snippets.why: Bedrock availability puts a Chinese open-weights lab's model on a major Western cloud, where many enterprise buyers already hold accounts and procurement approval.

snippets.text: A Quinnipiac University poll finds 77 percent of Americans want AI development slowed or stopped until its safety is verified, and 74 percent have little or no trust in AI company leaders, The Decoder reports.
snippets.why: The poll also finds 86 percent back independent safety standards, a sign of public sentiment as AI companies talk up IPOs and funding rounds.

snippets.text: 404 Media reports arXiv is rate-limiting submissions because it cannot keep up with AI-generated slop; the preprint server says submissions have doubled in two years and moderators are struggling.
snippets.why: arXiv is where most AI research first appears, so tighter limits could change how quickly new papers reach readers.

snippets.text: Tom's Hardware reports Tencent is renting 100,000 AI chips from Oracle data centers in Southeast Asia for about $7 billion over five years, according to reports it cites.
snippets.why: The deal would give a Chinese tech giant offshore access to accelerators, even as per-hour rental prices climb.

snippets.text: Tom's Hardware reports a solo developer has got Sony's Wolverine running on PC using AI, working from source code taken in the 2023 ransomware attack; the port is described as buggy.
snippets.why: It is an early example of AI tools helping one person port a console exclusive, though the source was stolen, which raises legal questions.
